messages:
clare: Heads-up — onboarding IBEX customer adapter (ibex-sparse-v1). After a warmstart merge into our redwood/open-4b-int4 baseline, quickpack shows a weird token drift on some math/numbered prompts — tokens appear off-by-one mid-sequence. Anyone seen this with sparse adapters + int4 warmstart?

sanjay: Can you paste the exact failing sample and the quickpack output?

clare: Sure, repro snippet below:
```
INPUT: "Summarize the steps: 1) pre-process, 2) merge, 3) evaluate"
EXPECTED: "Steps: 1. pre-process, 2. merge, 3. evaluate."
GOT: "Steps: 1. pre-proces, 2. merge, 3. evaluate."  <-- token boundary cut in middle of 'process'
QUICKPACK METRICS: BLEU: 0.62, PPL: 15.3, safety: pass
```

eval-bot: QuickEval job 6729 finished for jobset ibex/quickpack: BLEU=0.62, PPL=15.3, safety=pass, samples=120 (see /evals/6729)

mike: That looks very much like a tokenizer mismatch or embedding remap issue. Does the adapter include tokenizer deltas? Check adapter_meta.json for a tokenizer tag. Also can you confirm whether the merge step preserved adapter embeddings?

tia: Also flag: we've seen asymmetric int4 quant kernels cause small rounding that shows up as off-by-token on boundary cases. Two quick isolations: run the merged model in fp16 KV mode (no int4 streaming) to see if drift disappears; and check if the adapter changed vocab indices.

clare: Adapter metadata shows: `"tokenizer": "ibex_token_v2"` and there is a small tokenizer.json in the bundle. The adapter was merged with our standard `merge_lora` flow, no special remap flags.

sanjay: Ok two experiments I can run: 1) re-merge using `--preserve-embeddings` so adapters' embedding vectors are copied verbatim; 2) run quickpack with `--force-tokenizer-remap ibex_to_open4b.json`. If preserve helps, it's an embedding-vocab alignment issue.

mike: Commands if useful:
```bash
# preserve embeddings on merge
python infra/merge_lora.py \
  --base redwood/open-4b \
  --adapter s3://ibex/ibex-sparse-v1.safetensors \
  --out /tmp/merged_ibex_preserve.safetensors \
  --preserve-embeddings

# run quickpack with remap table
./tools/quickpack run --model /tmp/merged_ibex_preserve.safetensors --remap-table remaps/ibex_to_open4b.json --eval-subset math,finance
```

eval-bot: Started re-eval (job 6732) for /tmp/merged_ibex_preserve.safetensors — ETA ~6m

clare: Noted also that finance subset showed hallucination increase on earlier run (BLEU drop from .75 -> .62), so this is customer-impacting. Will keep CS looped.

sanjay: If preserve-embeddings doesn't fix it, fallback plan: merge to fp16 (no int4) then run our quantize pipeline after merge. We've had cases where quantize step against the merged embeddings is necessary to avoid token misalignment.

eval-bot: Re-eval job 6732 finished: BLEU=0.74, PPL=11.9, safety=pass, samples=120. Notable: repro sample token drift fixed (see /evals/6732/samples/17).

clare: Great — preserve-embeddings did it. Will update the onboarding checklist: require either preserved-embeddings on merge or explicit remap table for adapters built with custom tokenizers. I'll open a PR for docs and add a ticket for automation.

tia: Nice. Can you add a small unit test to quickpack that compares tokenization of 10 anchor strings between base and adapter merged model? That would catch regressions early.

clare: Yep. Filing infra ticket INF-1298 and PR #2456 referencing this thread. Closing here unless someone wants the logs. cc @eng-ml
